summary.oneLiner: Scoda Tubes navigated a volatile Q4FY26 marked by a 15-day gas-induced plant shutdown that capped revenue, yet delivered 22% PAT growth for FY26 while executing a strategic pivot into welded pipes for data centers and power. The core investment thesis rests on the H2FY27 commissioning of 13,000 MT welded capacity and a conservative 25% FY27 revenue guidance, which management admits is achievable even without pending large-scale power sector tenders.

one-line thesis: Scoda Tubes navigated a volatile Q4FY26 marked by a 15-day gas-induced plant shutdown that capped revenue, yet delivered 22% PAT growth for FY26 while executing a strategic pivot into welded pipes for data centers and power. The core investment thesis rests on the H2FY27 commissioning of 13,000 MT welded capacity and a conservative 25% FY27 revenue guidance, which management admits is achievable even without pending large-scale power sector tenders.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 518.7 Cr (+7% YoY); Q4 flat at INR 123.6 Cr due to gas shutdown. EBITDA: INR 76.2 Cr (14.7% margin vs 16.1% prior year) due to under-absorbed fixed costs from low utilization. PAT: INR 38.8 Cr (+22% YoY); Q4 PAT INR 6.3 Cr (-7% YoY). Order Book: INR 175 Cr (3-4 month visibility). Net Debt: Rising; peak debt expected ~INR 250 Cr in FY27 due to capex. One-offs: Q4 revenue impacted by ~INR 15-20 Cr loss from 15-day gas curtailment; raw material costs up 25-30% but fully passed through.
guidance: FY27 Revenue growth: 25% (conservative); EBITDA Margin: 14-15%; Order Inflow: Awaiting BHEL/NTPC tenders (shifted to June/July); Capex: INR 100 Cr planned for FY27 (Welded expansion + Solar).
order book & pipeline: INR 175 Crores representing 3-4 months of production; heavily weighted towards seamless; no long-dated power orders yet as BHEL tender delayed; inquiries strong for welded data center applications but no booked orders until H2FY27 commissioning.
segment / subsidiary detail: Seamless: 20,000 MT capacity (70% utilization target FY27); Mother Hollow: 70% captive consumption targeting 100% by FY28. Welded: Current ~1,000 MT expanding to 13,000 MT by Q2FY27 (trial) and 21,150 MT by H1FY28; targeted for data centers, HVAC, water treatment.
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into Data Center cooling/HVAC market via welded pipes (up to 16-inch diameter); Potential BHEL/NTPC thermal power tenders (50 GW government target); Export mix expansion (currently 34.6% FY26, targeting 40%).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margins compressed to 14.7% (FY26) from 16.1% due to startup costs and gas shutdown; Power/Fuel is 17-18% of total expenses; Gas prices up 25% but passed through; Solar project (8.79 MW) expected to save INR 8.63 Cr/year, boosting future margins.
capex / expansion: FY26 Spend: INR 110 Cr. FY27 Plan: ~INR 100 Cr. Breakdown: INR 45 Cr for initial 13,000 MT welded line; INR 40 Cr for additional 8,000 MT welded line; INR 40 Cr approx for solar installations across both plants. Funding: Internal accruals, term loans, and remaining IPO proceeds (INR 74.2 Cr cash on hand).
capital allocation: No equity dilution planned; Debt to increase by ~INR 50 Cr in FY27 to fund capex before deleveraging post-utilization; Focus on working capital normalization (inventory days reducing from 217 to 160).
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical supply chain delays (machinery from China delayed to July/August); Gas price volatility and availability; Delay in BHEL/NTPC power sector tenders; Execution risk on welded plant commissioning; High inventory days during transition.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about Q4 operational hiccups (gas); Conservative on guidance (admitting upside potential); Defensive on competitive data (refusing volume/realization disclosures); Confident on technology shift from extruded to pierced seamless pipes.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly noted a industry-wide procurement policy shift where major buyers like BHEL and BARC are now accepting hot-pierced pipes over traditionally preferred hot-extruded pipes, expanding Scoda's addressable market in power/nuclear sectors. Cancellation of European acquisition due to impending 50% import quota and safeguard duty hike makes domestic expansion the sole growth vector.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for specialized cooling pipes in rapid data center expansion; current supply limited to smaller diameters. | Scoda Tubes Limited | beneficiary | High | New welded capacity (16-inch capability) directly targets this gap; inquiries already received; commissioning H2FY27 aligns with sector capex cycle. |
| Thermal power capacity addition targets (50 GW) require massive tube volumes; tender delays create uncertainty. | Scoda Tubes Limited | beneficiary | Med | Approved vendor for BHEL/NTPC; shift to accepting pierced pipes is a structural tailwind, but revenue recognition depends on tender release timing (expected June/July). |
| Rising energy costs squeezing margins for power-intensive manufacturers. | Scoda Tubes Limited | beneficiary | Med | 8.79 MW solar captive power project provides a distinct cost advantage (~INR 8.6 Cr annual savings) relative to peers lacking similar integration. |

themes.title: Steel tubes & building-materials capex beneficiaries
themes.need: Domestic capex + import-substitution lift value-added steel tubes/pipes and building materials - APLAPOLLO/HITECH/JTLIND/SURYAROSNI/SAMBHV/VENUSPIPES on structural & SS tubes (solar structures, DC cooling, API), FINPIPE/SUPREMEIND/APOLLOPIPE on PVC pipes, MAANALU on aluminium extrusions, RATNAVEER on SS fasteners. A data-center-cooling adjacency adds margin optionality.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Fully integrated manufacturer of SS seamless and SS welded products" — SS seamless pipes, seamless tubes, seamless "U" tubes, instrumentation tubes, and welded tubes / "U" tubes — with dedicated seamless and welded divisions at a single manufacturing facility in Gujarat.
- The deck frames seven "Sustainable Moats": specialised SS production, customer diversification and international presence, strategic location plus fully integrated production, extensive quality control, international accreditations and product approvals, an experienced and qualified team, and consistent financial performance.
- Accreditation stack is a stated barrier: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018; ASTM, ASME and EN manufacturing standards; PED 2014/68/EU and ADW/AD 2000-Merkblatt-W0 for products sold to Europe; plus DNV-CP-0252, DNV Marine and Indian Boiler Regulation. Bureau Veritas Marine (France) and Rina Marine (Italy) have been applied for.
- Approval-led customer base built over 15+ years: BHEL (HEEP Haridwar, Hyderabad, Bhopal and Jhansi), EIL, HPCL, GNFC, IFFCO (Kandla and Kalol), KRIBHCO, BEML, NTPC Bilaspur, Triveni Turbine, Laxmi Organics, the Department of Atomic Energy (GoI), and Indian Railways units including Banaras Locomotive Works, Rail Coach Factory, Modern Coach Factory and Chittaranjan Locomotive Works.
- "Company's capabilities and accreditations have enabled Scoda Tubes to cater to 349 clients globally till date", with a stated presence in 32 countries and exports to 32 countries since inception.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Transient Q1 disruptions] Management attributes the quarter's weakness to a temporary gas-supply disruption at the manufacturing facility during April that affected production "for a couple of weeks", challenging manpower availability, global supply-chain disruption raising freight costs, and raw-material price volatility — all described as "largely transient in nature" with corrective measures taken and gas supply restored.
- [FY27 guidance reaffirmed] "We remain committed to achieving our FY27 guidance as operations continue to stabilize and production ramps up at our seamless facility" — the guidance itself is not quantified anywhere in the deck.
- [Industry — global] Global SS pipes and tubes demand grew at a CAGR of ~3% from CY19–CY23 and is expected to grow at 3–4% between CY23–CY28, reaching 3.7 mn tonnes in CY28E from 3.1 mn tonnes in CY23; oil and gas (23–26% in CY2023, 24–27% in CY2028E) and process industries (18–21% to 19–22%) dominate demand.
- [Industry — India] Indian SS tubes and pipes demand of 322 thousand tonnes in FY24 is projected at 450 thousand tonnes by FY29E, with process industry (28–32% of demand, 6–8% CAGR FY24–29), oil & gas (22–25%, 6–8%), ART (20–23%, 8–10%) and ABC (18–21%, 6–8%) as drivers; imports to India fell from 90 to 56 thousand tonnes and exports rose from 41 to 64 thousand tonnes between FY20 and FY24, and the deck adds that "policy protection through imposition of anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports will provide further fillip to local producers".
- [Promoter-family management] The senior team is family-led — Samarth B Patel (Chairperson & Executive Director, exports and marketing), Jagrut R Patel (Managing Director, domestic sales and marketing), Saurabh A Patel (Non-Executive Director, project development), Ravi R Patel (CFO) and Vipul A Patel (President), each cited with "10+ years of experience"; three independent directors are named.
